note: Every threshold is {value, reason}. A bare number is rejected by look_config.py: a threshold with no reason is a guess. All values are PROVISIONAL until a judged corpus exists to calibrate against (DESIGN.md AMENDMENT 2 B3/B5); the floor GATES, the model judges only REFINE (bus TRAPS s8: blinded agent image calls can sit near chance).

auto_exclude_symmetric.reason: OFF by default. A playback capture can include black window bars (the UM CUDA fixture tiles are 16:9 with ~25% black bars while the CPU tiles are content-only), and counting them as 'crushed shadows' fails the frame on geometry, not on look. But pixels alone cannot tell a capture bar from a genuinely crushed region of the scene: round-1 review produced both a one-sided and a symmetric dark band that read as bars and let a crushed frame PASS. So nothing is hidden from the floor unless the caller DECLARES it (--letterbox-bars top=N,bottom=N) or opts in to symmetric auto-detection (--letterbox auto-symmetric); the choice is written into every frame verdict. Undeclared, the full frame is measured, so a barred capture fails 'crushed shadows' loudly instead of passing quietly.

bar_max_code.reason: A band counts as a bar only if its brightest channel code is <= this value on EVERY pixel of the band. 4 (not 0) tolerates resampling ringing at the bar edge on downscaled thumbnails; a real picture row is never that dark across its full width unless it is a bar.

min_active_px.reason: Never crop to nothing: below this many remaining rows/columns the frame is treated as having no detectable letterbox.

max_excluded_pct.reason: If an exclusion (declared or auto-symmetric) would discard more than half of the frame it is more likely a genuinely dark frame than a letterbox; refuse to exclude, measure the full frame and say so in the verdict instead of silently shrinking the measured area.

symmetry_tolerance_px.reason: Auto-symmetric detection applies bars only when the two opposite bars (top and bottom, or left and right) differ by at most this many pixels; a thumbnail resample can leave one anti-aliased edge row on one side. A dark band on ONE side only is scene content (crushed sky, a black stage, a dark foreground reaching an edge), never a bar.

clipped_highlight_pct_max.reason: DESIGN.md B3: clipped highlights <= 1% of the active frame. Definition reuses make-contact-sheet.py channel_stats (luma >= 254 on 8-bit) so the number is comparable with every existing stats sidecar.

crushed_shadow_pct_max.reason: DESIGN.md B3: crushed shadows <= 2% of the active frame. Definition reuses make-contact-sheet.py channel_stats (luma <= 1 on 8-bit); measured on the active area so letterbox bars do not count.

mean_saturation_max.reason: Saturation ceiling (a): mean HSV saturation over the active frame. Natural footage and a restrained grade sit well below this; a Look Assist mapping that pushes the MEAN past 0.55 is oversaturating the whole frame. Provisional: the two tracked fixtures read ~0.08.

oversaturated_pixel_pct_max.reason: Saturation ceiling (b): share of pixels with HSV saturation >= oversaturated_sat_min AND value >= oversaturated_value_min. A small neon highlight is legitimate; more than 3% of the frame is a colour blow-out that the mean alone can hide.

oversaturated_sat_min.reason: HSV saturation at or above which a pixel counts as oversaturated for oversaturated_pixel_pct_max.

oversaturated_value_min.reason: Pixels darker than this HSV value are excluded from the oversaturation count: saturation of near-black pixels is sensor noise amplified by the HSV division, not colour.

skin_min_pixel_pct.reason: A skin-tone region smaller than 1% of the active frame is too few pixels to give a stable mean hue; the skin check is then NOT_APPLICABLE (never a pass).

skin_hue_drift_deg_max.reason: DESIGN.md B3: skin-hue drift <= ~5 degrees where skin is present. A drift needs a baseline (the same frame without the look, or the other backend): absolute skin hue varies by subject, so with no reference frame the check is NOT_APPLICABLE and the absolute offset is only reported.

skin_region_retain_fraction.reason: When the BASELINE has a usable skin-tone region, the subject must keep at least this fraction of that region's share of the frame. A look that pushes skin out of the colour box (green, magenta, grey) empties the subject's own mask; reading that as 'no skin, not applicable' would let the worst colour shift pass, so a lost or shrunken region is a FAIL.

skin_baseline_crop_tolerance_px.reason: Drift is measured over the BASELINE's skin mask when the two active areas match after a centre crop of at most this many pixels per axis (a downscaled thumbnail keeps an anti-aliased edge row). Beyond that the mask cannot be aligned and the drift falls back to each frame's own region, which the verdict records (maskBasis).

cb_range.reason: Chai & Ngan (1999) YCbCr skin-tone chroma box, Cb axis.

cr_range.reason: Chai & Ngan (1999) YCbCr skin-tone chroma box, Cr axis.

min_luma.reason: Chroma of very dark pixels is noise; excluded from the skin-tone region.

hue_range_deg.reason: HSV hue window that real skin occupies; intersected with the YCbCr box to reject colours that only satisfy the chroma box (e.g. desaturated greens).

sat_range.reason: HSV saturation window of skin; excludes greys and fully saturated oranges.

geometry_tolerance_px.reason: CUDA and CPU frames of one clip at one scale must have identical active-area geometry; a different size means a different render or crop and the pair is GEOMETRY_MISMATCH, not a number. The fixture demo (downscaled thumbnails) overrides this explicitly and the override is written into the verdict.

mismatch_channel_tolerance.reason: A pixel is a MISMATCH when any channel differs by more than this many 8-bit codes. Float-on-GPU vs integer-on-CPU rounding across a chain of look stages lands within a few codes; larger differences are real stage differences.

gated.reason: A3: the stages the display shader implements must match the CPU render tightly, so this scope GATES.

mean_abs_delta_max.reason: Per-channel mean absolute difference, 8-bit codes: rounding-level agreement.

max_abs_delta_max.reason: Reported, not gated: a single outlier pixel (an edge, a hot pixel) dominates the maximum; mismatch_fraction_max gates instead.

mismatch_fraction_max.reason: At most 2% of pixels may differ by more than mismatch_channel_tolerance.

ssim_min.reason: Luma SSIM (Gaussian 11x11, sigma 1.5, K1=0.01, K2=0.03): two renders of the same stages should be structurally near-identical.

gated.reason: A3: REPORTED, not gated, until the CUDA display shader carries every look stage (L2 CUDA-LOOK-DISPLAY-STAGES-1). The verdict still says whether the shader-subset numbers would have been met.

mean_abs_delta_max.reason: Same reference numbers as shader-subset, shown so the gap to the gated bar is visible.

min_choices.reason: Below 6 non-tie slot choices a binomial test cannot separate a biased judge from a coin; the tally reports INSUFFICIENT_N instead of a verdict on the judge.

alpha.reason: Two-sided exact binomial p-value below which a judge's left/right split is flagged as slot bias.

min_consistent_units.reason: A judge's preference is readable only with at least this many real units whose two orderings agree. Under a coin-flip judge a unanimous 3-unit vote happens 25% of the time and a 2-unit one 50%; 4 is the smallest floor that rules out the degenerate sessions. It is NOT a significance claim: a 4-0 vote still has an exact two-sided p of 0.125, which the entry reports as votePValue.

third_judge_points.reason: DESIGN.md B4: two judges more than 1 rubric point apart (on any criterion, for any subject) need a third judge.
